claim: The entorhinal cortex is involved in establishing enduring visuo-auditory associative memory in the neocortex.
source: The entorhinal cortex is involved in establishing enduring visuo-auditory associative memory in the neocortex.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a premise for the study.

claim: High-frequency laser stimulation (HFS laser) of the visuo-auditory projection did not induce long-term potentiation.
source: High-frequency laser stimulation (HFS laser) of the visuo-auditory projection did not induce long-term potentiation.
evidence: This finding is reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: After pairing with sound stimulus, the visuo-auditory inputs were potentiated following infusion of cholecystokinin (CCK).
source: However, after pairing with sound stimulus, the visuo-auditory inputs were potentiated following either infusion of cholecystokinin (CCK) or HFS laser of the entorhino-auditory CCK-expressing projection.

claim: After pairing with sound stimulus, the visuo-auditory inputs were potentiated following HFS laser of the entorhino-auditory CCK-expressing projection.

claim: Cck expression is higher in entorhinal cortex neurons projecting to the auditory cortex than in those originating from the visual cortex.
source: Combining retrograde tracing and RNAscope in situ hybridization, we show that Cck expression is higher in entorhinal cortex neurons projecting to the auditory cortex than in those originating from the visual cortex.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4E.

claim: In the presence of CCK, potentiation in the neocortex occurred when the presynaptic input arrived 200 ms before postsynaptic firing, even after just five trials of pairing.
source: In the presence of CCK, potentiation in the neocortex occurred when the presynaptic input arrived 200 ms before postsynaptic firing, even after just five trials of pairing.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5C.

claim: Inactivation of the CCK+ projection from the entorhinal cortex to the auditory cortex blocked the formation of visuo-auditory associative memory.
source: Behaviorally, inactivation of the CCK+ projection from the entorhinal cortex to the auditory cortex blocked the formation of visuo-auditory associative memory.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by behavioral data in Figure 6B.

claim: Neocortical visuo-auditory association is formed through heterosynaptic plasticity, which depends on release of CCK in the neocortex mostly from entorhinal afferents.
source: Our results indicate that neocortical visuo-auditory association is formed through heterosynaptic plasticity, which depends on release of CCK in the neocortex mostly from entorhinal afferents.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing multiple experimental findings.

claim: Cross-modal association is crucial for our brain to integrate information from different modalities.
source: Cross-modal association is crucial for our brain to integrate information from different modalities.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Cross-modal association is fundamental for creating complete and context-rich memories.
source: This integrated processing is fundamental for creating complete and context-rich memories.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Cross-modal association is assumed to mainly occur in higher-order association cortices as evidenced by anatomical studies.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Neurons in the auditory cortex (AC) start to respond to light stimuli after a classical fear conditioning, coupling light and electrical stimulation (ES) of the AC.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: This type of association can be blocked by inactivation of the entorhinal cortex (EC).

claim: Removal of the bilateral medial temporal lobe, where the EC locates, prevents the formation of long-term declarative memory in patient H.M.

claim: The EC is strongly and reciprocally connected with both the hippocampus and neocortex.
source: The EC is strongly and reciprocally connected with both the hippocampus and neocortex (Canto et al., 2008; Swanson and Köhler, 1986), and rich in cholecystokinin (CCK)-positive neurons, both in rat (Greenwood et al., 1981; Innis et al., 1979; Köhler and Chan-Palay, 1982) and mouse (Meziane et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The EC is rich in cholecystokinin (CCK)-positive neurons, both in rat and mouse.
source: The EC is strongly and reciprocally connected with both the hippocampus and neocortex (Canto et al., 2008; Swanson and Köhler, 1986), and rich in cholecystokinin (CCK)-positive neurons, both in rat (Greenwood et al., 1981; Innis et al., 1979; Köhler and Chan-Palay, 1982) and mouse (Meziane et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: CCK is the most abundant neuropeptide in brain.
source: As the most abundant neuropeptide in brain (Beinfeld et al., 1981; Dockray et al., 1978; Innis et al., 1979; Larsson and Rehfeld, 1979; Rehfeld, 1978; Vanderhaeghen et al., 1980), sulphated cholecystokinin octapeptide (CCK-8S) was shown to have excitatory effects on pyramidal neurons (Dodd and Kelly, 1981) and plays an important role in learning and memory (Horinouchi et al., 2004; Lo et al., 2008; Meziane et al., 1993; Nomoto et al., 1999; Tsutsumi et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.
